subject: Port existing Distance 6 or Distance 7 projects to R

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Port existing Distance 6 or Distance 7 projects to R
parts:
Group friends

Do you have projects you have built in Distance 6 or Distance 7? Are you
curious about analysing these distance sampling surveys using R? If so,
we have some news.

Dave Miller has developed an R package called 'readdst'. The purpose of
this package is to read Distance projects (these projects as you know
use the '.dst' extension, hence the name readdst). Distance projects
effectively store not only data, but also model definitions and data
filters in Access-like databases. Dave's package reads these databases
and converts the data to forms readable by R as well as calls to the
'mrds' package for fitting detection functions and producing abundance
estimates.

The 'readdst' package does not live on CRAN, but you can install it to
your R installation from its Github repository via the function
'install_github()' in the devtools package.

library(devtools)
install_github("DistanceDevelopment/readdst")

A case study showing the use of 'readdst' is available on the
'distancesampling.org' website, along with other vignettes for analysing
distance data in R.

Look at the bottom of this distancesampling.org page
http://distancesampling.org/R/index.html under 'Migrating data and
analyses from Distance for Windows to R environment'.

The 'readdst' package has limitations; it cannot properly migrate
projects that use multipliers or post-stratification. It does not cope
with 'dsm', 'mads' or 'DSsim' projects.

We welcome your feedback.
